title: Network Rail credits AI-powered DeterTech cameras with cutting trespass at Dingwall's canal level crossings from about five incidents a day in June 2025
summary: Network Rail release (9 Jun 2026): June 2025 data showed five trespass incidents a day between Dingwall Canal North and South crossings; after cameras that detect route departures, issue audio warn...
account: In a media release for International Level Crossing Awareness Day on 9 Jun 2026, Network Rail's Scotland's Railway said data from June 2025 had shown an average of five trespass incidents a day at Dingwall, where people used the railway bridge over the River Peffery as a shortcut between the Dingwall Canal North and South level crossings. It stated that following the introduction of AI-powered DeterTech cameras, which detect when someone leaves the designated route, issue an audio warning and send live images to Network Rail and British Transport Police for a rapid response, incidents had reduced, alongside new anti-trespass signage, campaigns and minor improvements; it also said incidents were starting to rise again as the weather improved. Rachel Shaw, Network Rail's head of operational safety, spoke of a big drop in trespass at Dingwall, and BTP Inspector Ashley Forbes said worrying levels of trespass were still being seen. No post-deployment count, installation date or individual detection leading to a train stop or police attendance is given; the release is the deployer's own account; the BBC (10 Jun 2026) and the Ross-shire Journal (9 Jun 2026) relayed the same account, and neither names the supplier or gives a post-installation count. The BBC (2 Jul 2025) had reported Network Rail's CCTV of people using the bridge as a shortcut, with trains passing at up to 65mph. The date given is the publication date.
purpose: The cameras are built to detect people leaving the designated route, warn them and alert Network Rail and police in real time.
system: DeterTech AI-powered cameras with audio warnings and live image relay
deployer: Network Rail (Scotland's Railway) with British Transport Police
taxonomy_note: No type covers trespass prevention; chosen because the gain is fewer incidents for the infrastructure manager and police to respond to. A person-on-track variant of this case was previously rejected for lacking any detection-to-stop event; this record is the aggregate claim, which rests on a single deployer release without a post-deployment figure.

ratings.reason: The release reports a reduction without numbers and notes incidents rising again.
No quantified operational outcome is documented.

ai_role.statement: The release attributes the reduction to the cameras together with signage and campaigns; detection counts, false alarms and responses are not reported, and the cameras' AI is described only as detecting route departures.
